reports.title: The amount of investment gains (losses) in any given quarter is usually meaningless and delivers figures for net earnings per share that can be extremely misleading to investors who have little or no knowledge of accounting rules.

desk.headline: Operating earnings down 6% to $12.7bn as insurance underwriting weakened; $9.6bn of buybacks; no guidance

numbers.eps_basis: GAAP net earnings per average Class B share

results: Operating earnings (excluding investment gains) fell 6% to $12.7bn; net earnings fell 28% to $22.1bn because investment gains were smaller than a year ago.
Insurance was the weak spot: underwriting profit dropped to $1.35bn from $2.37bn and insurance investment income fell 14% to $2.73bn.
The operating businesses grew: BNSF railroad +19% to $1.73bn, Berkshire Hathaway Energy +8% to $1.61bn, manufacturing, service and retailing +12% to $4.04bn.
Berkshire bought back about $9.6bn of its own shares in the quarter ($14.4bn year to date); insurance float rose to about $178.5bn.
Net earnings per Class A share were $15,502 (Class B $10.33), down from $21,413 ($14.28).

guidance.summary: Berkshire gives no earnings guidance. The release warns that quarterly investment gains are usually meaningless for judging the business.

call.source: No call coverage found — Berkshire does not hold a results call

watch: Whether insurance underwriting (including Geico, which raised advertising spend) recovers from this quarter's drop.
The pace of share buybacks, which the press noted had likely slowed as the share price rose.
Continued growth at BNSF, the energy business and the manufacturing, service and retail group.

sources.title: Berkshire Hathaway buys back $9.6 billion of its own stock but its profits declined — Associated Press (via NY1), 7 Nov 2026
